note: Figure 5(b), FeTe0.65Se0.35, H // c-axis. TEN isotherms: five for sample A (black open symbols) and five for sample B (red filled symbols). Temperature is carried by marker SHAPE, not colour, so the colour-keyed extractor cannot separate the five isotherms of one sample on colour alone. Each series is therefore confined to its own curve by a per-series staircase of exclusion boxes whose step boundaries are the midlines between neighbouring same-colour curves, measured column by column from the rendered crop: the upper member of a neighbouring pair keeps what lies above the staircase, the lower member what lies below. All five sample-A curves are recovered this way. The curves never cross, so at every field the black traces sort top-to-bottom as 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 K; the three hottest end early (9 K near 54000 Oe, 10 K near 29700 Oe, 11 K near 15700 Oe) and each series is blanked to the right of its own last marker so a shorter isotherm cannot inherit the tail of a longer one. The x axis is in Oe (0 to 70000); first_major and last_major are given in TESLA (10 kOe = 1 T) so the output is in tesla. The x majors at 0 and 70000 Oe sit on the frame corners and are not walked, so the detected majors run 10000 to 60000 Oe, i.e. 1 to 6 T. There is no text layer on this page, so every annotation - legend, panel label, H//c-axis, the two sample labels and their arrows - is excluded by an explicit box.
